scope: Restore sourced nonlinear horizontal hull terms already present in the original MMG idea; no new states, new free parameters or hydrodynamic solve
reason: Numerically converged geometric-input pilot improves45deg yaw amplitude and beam sway, but excites an overly weakly damped slow yaw mode. Current source-total linear derivatives omit the same source's nonlinear velocity terms. Restore exactly those fixed Table13 Appended terms before considering any new empirical residual input.
source: Franceschi etal2021 DOI10.3390/jmse9060665 p25 Table13, Appended. Image checked. Same close-but-not-identical loading and18/20kn caveat as source total linear block.
normalization: v_mid=v_CG+0.683*r; vprime=v_mid/U, rprime=r*L/U. Force=.5rhoU²L² times X/Y, moment=.5rhoU²L³ times N; N_CG=N_mid+0.683Y. source starboard/down vs our port/up both Y,N reverse; all odd lateral polynomial terms have invariant coefficients.
ownership: Add only quadratic/cubic terms to the source-total linear velocity closure; no linear derivatives, added mass, passive foils or control gains duplicated. Roll equation and its calibrated parameters stay unchanged. One-way conditional roll remains explicit.
steady_trim: Center nonlinear forces for fluctuation statistics at the observed prescribed mean speed/heading. Do not claim prediction of mean speed loss or mean trim equilibrium.
solver: Periodic full-record fixed point using existing linear inverse, numerical relaxation0.25, maximum60iterations, relative RMS iterate residual1e-3 in all response channels with floor1e-5SI for u,v and1e-6rad for psi,r. Relaxation is a numerical method, not physical coefficient. No best-iteration selection; failure remains nonconverged.
physical_candidate: Combined geometric increments plus all fixed sourced nonlinear terms, not selection of whichever subterm scores best.
no_automatic_admission: Converged numerics alone are not physical validation. Report amplitude, period, all channels and loading/controller limitations.
